blocks.text: Russian has two words for *you*. **Ты** is for one person you know well — family, friends, children, pets. **Вы** is for anyone you would address formally, and for more than one person. When in doubt, say **вы**: it is never rude.
*Как тебя зовут?* means, word for word, *How do they call you?* — so the answer is **Меня зовут …**, *They call me …*. The name stays as it is; the person (**меня**, *me*) changes.

items: Как тебя зовут? — Меня зовут Ива́н.
What's your name? — My name is Ivan.
Как вас зовут? — Меня зовут А́нна Петро́вна.
What is your name? — Anna Petrovna.
Как дела? — Хорошо́, спаси́бо. А у тебя?
How are things? — Good, thanks. And you?

blocks.text: **Кто э́то?** asks *who is this?* — **Что э́то?** asks *what is this?* The answer needs no verb: **Это Ма́ша.** *This is Masha.*
Russians address people they respect by first name and patronymic — **Анна Петровна**, **Ива́н Серге́евич** — and with **вы**.

exercises.q: You meet your new boss. How do you say hello?
exercises.why: **Здравствуйте** is the formal hello — right for a boss, a stranger, or more than one person.

exercises.q: Your little cousin asks your name. Which question did she ask?
exercises.why: A child speaks to you with **ты**, so she uses **тебя**.
The answer copies the question: **Меня** зовут …, *they call me* …

exercises.q: Which word asks about a person?

exercises.why: **Пока** is the informal goodbye; **До свидания** is the polite one.
